name: Alsace grand cru Steinert

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this cool ripen Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer, Riesling, Pinot Noir and Müller-Thurgau fully without cooking off their freshness.
Gewürztraminer, Riesling, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity. Granite weathers to coarse, acid, free-draining soil that warms quickly and holds heat. Its acidity tends to lower the grapes' acidity, which suits Gamay.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.
Faces the morning sun. Early light dries the dew, which cuts disease, and the grapes are spared the hottest afternoon sun.

winkler: Only very early grapes ripen well, mostly hybrids and a few vinifera.
